topic.title: Projects for Contributors
topic.shortdesc: Contributors have read-only access to the projects they were added to, and work on the content of those projects in a personal workspace.

body.p: A project connects documentation work to a Git repository. As a Contributor, you can work with the content of a project, but the project itself is managed by its owners and maintainers.

section.title: Which Projects You Can See
section.p: The Projects page lists only the projects that a project owner explicitly added you to. This is true for public projects as well: unlike users with the Author platform user role, you do not automatically get access to the public projects of your organization.

To be added to a project, ask a project owner to add you on the Members page of that project. You are always added with the Collaborator project role, which is the only project role a Contributor can hold. You receive an email notification when this happens.

section.title: What You Can Do in a Project

ul.li: Browse the files of the project and read their content.
Edit the project files in your personal workspace.
Suggest your changes to the project team as a review task.
See the review tasks of the project and take part in them.

section.p: Your access to the project content is read-only. Nothing you do in your personal workspace changes the project itself until a project maintainer or owner integrates your proposal.

section.title: What Is Not Available
section.p: The parts of a project that change the project for everyone are not available to Contributors. The Settings and Members pages, the Deliverables page, and the branch management actions are reserved for project maintainers and owners.
